```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
records <- system.file("extdata", "benchmarks", package = "CerebroNexus", mustWork = TRUE)
read_tsv <- function(name) utils::read.delim(file.path(records, name), check.names = FALSE)
```

# Scope and evidence

This article separates expression access, CRB persistence, server preparation,
and browser rendering. Their timings have different boundaries and cannot be
added into an overall Viewer speedup. For backend selection, sidecar portability
and launching the demo, see [Working with large datasets](million_cell_crb_artifacts.html).

The recorded measurements below are **historical experiments**, not a new
5.0.0 benchmark. Correctness repairs and the current release have not been
remeasured under a complete matched large-data protocol. A passed regression
suite does not establish a performance result.

All tables and the Ren figure read the small, checked-in records under
`inst/extdata/benchmarks/`. These records are included in installed packages;
rendering this article requires neither a large dataset nor a developer cache.
Do not overwrite recorded experiments with a new run.

# Ren v2: expression backends

The recorded 2026-10-08 comparison used matching BPCells and HDF5 CRBs with
1,462,702 cells and 27,943 genes. Each backend ran in three fresh R processes,
with alternating backend order. A separate planning process froze a 12-gene
panel and reference value fingerprints. Every measurement verified identical
single-row and block values outside the timed expressions.

`startup_seconds` includes source-package loading and CRB loading. First-gene
latency is the first getter call in that process; repeated-gene latency is a
within-process median. The 12-gene block is materialized. A fresh process does
not imply a cold operating-system disk cache. These are R-side measurements,
not time until a browser page becomes usable. The retained TSV does not contain
a complete host/package manifest, limiting portability and exact environment
reproduction; future reruns must retain it alongside their observations.

```{r ren-results}
ren <- read_tsv("ren-backends-20261008.tsv")
stopifnot(all(ren$correctness == "OK"))
metrics <- c("startup_seconds", "first_gene_seconds", "hot_gene_p50_seconds", "twelve_gene_seconds")
ren_summary <- aggregate(ren[metrics], list(backend = ren$backend), stats::median)
knitr::kable(ren_summary, digits = 3)
```

```{r ren-figure, fig.width=12, fig.height=4, fig.cap="Historical Ren v2 comparison; medians of three fresh-process rounds. Backend computation, not browser page load."}
source(file.path(records, "plot-ren.R"), local = TRUE)
plotRenBackendBenchmark(ren)
```

On this workload, HDF5 has lower repeated single-gene latency, while BPCells has
lower materialized block latency. This does not establish a universal backend
ranking: storage orientation, query shape, data density and caching all matter.
In particular, results from older BPCells layouts must not be used to describe
the current gene-major layout without a matched rerun.

# Historical mouse-million experiments

The input was the official 10x E18 mouse-brain matrix (1,306,127 barcodes,
27,998 features), reduced deterministically to one million evenly spaced cells.
The preparation used a 50,000-cell sketch (seed 123), normalization, variable
features, 30-component PCA, neighbors, clustering at resolution 1 and UMAP,
then projected results to all selected cells. Counts used BPCells uint32
storage; thin RDS and qs2 CRBs reused the same sidecar.

The 2026-09-12 backend records used an Apple M1 Pro with 32 GiB RAM, macOS 27.0,
R 4.6.1 arm64, BPCells 0.3.1 and Seurat 5.5.1. Exact source revisions and repeat
counts are retained in `million_cell_backend_hot_paths_manifest.tsv`.
The column named `latest` in that historical file refers to its recorded
candidate `3fb88b8a`, **not the current checkout**. Baselines are `69893a2b`
and `27303f21`. The two baseline backend implementations were identical;
their repeated columns are not independent experiments.

## CRB lifecycle

Five alternating warm-cache rounds measured control-file size, writing,
physical decoding and hydrated reading. Hydration includes sidecar attachment
and canonical-cell checksum validation. It does not include browser rendering.

```{r crb-lifecycle}
lifecycle <- utils::read.csv(file.path(records, "million_cell_crb_pr165.csv"))
knitr::kable(lifecycle[, c("candidate", "size_mib", "write_median_ms",
  "decode_median_ms", "hydrated_median_ms")], digits = 2)
```

## Server hot paths

Three warm-cache repetitions measured filtering, canonical indexing and
expression reads, with equality checks before timing. Allocation describes R
allocations, not browser heap or whole-process RSS. A recorded zero-millisecond
value is below the timer resolution, not literally free computation.

```{r backend-hot-paths}
hot <- read_tsv("million_cell_backend_hot_paths.tsv")
knitr::kable(hot[, c("metric", "scale", "pr165_ms", "latest_ms",
  "pr165_alloc_mib", "latest_alloc_mib", "check")], digits = 1)
```

The accompanying `million_cell_backend_bundle.tsv` records historical Linked
bundle construction and JSON costs; it predates later geometry/resource changes.
Static HTTP geometry and metadata must be counted separately from WebSocket
payloads. A tiny primary message is not the complete network cost.

## Browser acceptance boundaries

Keep cold first entry, warm entry, revisit and repeated operations separate.
Record draw submission, GPU completion, painted acknowledgement and progressive
completion separately; global Shiny idle is not a substitute for page readiness.
The request must match the current dataset generation, identity and selection.
Use the same dataset, viewport, source revision, browser and initial state on
both sides. Record timing and memory profiles in separate runs.

The historical five-round browser series and its immutable candidate/fixture
identities remain under `tests/benchmarks/results/viewer/million_cell_pages_pr4_pr5_4_6_3*`.
Those records used macOS Chrome and an older completion boundary for Linked
Views. Later Windows Brave acceptance used **WSL R**, not Windows-native R.
Neither series can be pooled with the other. Durable results and limitations
are summarized in `tests/benchmarks/results/viewer/PR184_ACCEPTANCE.md` in a repository checkout.
Stable Gene first usability below three seconds has not been established, and
there is no matched current-release, all-page speedup claim.

# Earlier exploratory pilot

The 2026-07-30 embedded/BPCells/HDF5 sweep is retained under
the retired pilot (see `tests/benchmarks/results/expression-backends/PRELIMINARY_BACKEND_RESULTS.md`). It used real mouse-brain and
human-PFC counts, synthetic grouping/embeddings, and contiguous cell blocks.
The macOS arm64 host had 32 GB RAM. The run preceded balanced independent
repeats and complete provenance; its tables and figures are exploratory.

Its useful lesson is that dense realization and construction of a large
in-memory Seurat object can dominate memory before a backend is written.
Cell count alone is not a memory budget: density and nonzero count matter.
Do not generalize its approximately 53 bytes/nonzero peak or old backend
ranking to current streaming exports. Raw pilot CSVs remain available for
inspection; current figure scripts intentionally require validated repeated
runs instead of treating this pilot as release evidence.

# Reproduce figures without rerunning measurements

From a repository checkout, with R installed:

```{bash, eval=FALSE}
Rscript tests/benchmarks/viewer/scripts/plot_ren_backend_acceptance.R   inst/extdata/benchmarks/ren-backends-20261008.tsv ren-backends.png
```

The command and the figure above share `inst/extdata/benchmarks/plot-ren.R` and
the same TSV. It only reads small recorded data and writes the figure; no atlas
download, Shiny session or benchmark is launched. To render this entire article,
install the checkout and run `rmarkdown::render()` on this Rmd.

# Optionally rerun measurements

Measurement scripts are retained in Git but excluded from R package builds.
These commands require a **repository checkout**, its declared dependencies,
and sufficient storage; they do not work from an installed package alone.
Record `git rev-parse HEAD`, `sessionInfo()`, host/browser versions and artifact
checksums with every new output. Save new runs outside the recorded-data directory.

For the mouse preparation, allow at least 16 GiB free disk for the recorded
artifact layout, additional space for parallel backends/outputs, and tens of
minutes or longer depending on hardware and downloads. The source alone is
about 3.93 GiB. Full Ren preparation has separate large download/storage costs;
inspect the preparation script and available disk before starting it. Do not
use an arbitrary memory limit or a historical completion time as a guarantee.

```{r prepare-mouse, eval=FALSE}
source("tests/benchmarks/viewer/scripts/prepare_viewer_1m_data.R")
pkgload::load_all(".")
crb <- prepareViewer1mBenchmarkData()
```

```{bash, eval=FALSE}
# Two already-prepared CRBs of the same Ren v2 expression data; three rounds.
Rscript tests/benchmarks/viewer/scripts/benchmark_ren_expression_backends.R   /data/ren-bpcells.crb /data/ren-h5.crb /results/ren-backends 3

# CRB lifecycle, five alternating rounds on the same sidecar.
Rscript tests/benchmarks/viewer/scripts/benchmark_million_cell_crb.R   /data/cerebro_mouse_brain_1m.crb 5 /results/crb-lifecycle.csv

# Resource-checked repeated expression-backend experiment.
bash tests/benchmarks/expression-backends/run.sh
```

A Ren comparison on already-prepared artifacts usually needs minutes rather
than the complete preparation workflow; actual duration remains host-dependent.
A full repeated export/access sweep can take hours. Its resource preflight
records memory, sparse-index and disk constraints before bulk transfer.
See `tests/benchmarks/viewer/README.md` for explicit page/renderer harness arguments and
`tests/benchmarks/expression-backends/README.md` for experimental units, profiling and publication
gates. Preserve raw rounds, source identities, failed observations and limits;
never replace them with a single favorable timing.
